lesson: Shared-site binding is a stored relationship between a link instance and a site of the linked model, not a property of its position. Linking by shared coordinates creates it; moving never creates it, and moving a bound link rewrites the linked model's coordinates. For file links the API can bind an in-place instance (PublishCoordinates with the link location id); for cloud links it cannot, so the bound state is reachable only by re-creating the instance, which deletes what is attached to it. A repair must never move a bound link, must decide between re-creating and keeping an unbound one by what depends on it, and must report what it could not bind.
rule:
1. Identity: loaded link -> GetLinkDocument().GetCloudModelPath() GUIDs; unloaded ACC link -> ExternalResourceReference.GetReferenceInformation() LinkedModelProjectId / LinkedModelModelId (observed 2024.3); file reference only for file-based links; name only when no identity can be read, and never over a link whose identity is known to be another model.
2. Load governed links before checking placement or binding (RevitLinkType.Load): an unloaded link always reads '<Not Shared>'. In a batch open all worksets; run with no other open document that has the same links loaded.
3. Check the host's active site first (Create Shared places relative to it, FP74). Then per instance: bound and in place -> nothing; bound and off position -> do NOT move (it would rewrite the link's site, FP72), report a host/link coordinate mismatch; unbound with nothing attached (GetDependentElements without the instance and its internal elements) -> create the new instance with ImportPlacement.Shared FIRST, apply workset and room bounding, pin, verify position AND binding, then delete the old one, in a SubTransaction; unbound with dependents -> keep the instance, move it into place if needed (safe while unbound), pin, and report the binding as unresolved; for a file link exactly in place PublishCoordinates(new LinkElementId(instance, link active location id)) can bind it, verify the link's site values unchanged.
4. Count what depends on each instance before deciding, and report what a re-creation removed.
5. Register an IFailuresPreprocessor on every repair transaction (delete warnings, list them in the report); a run with anything unfixable or unresolved says so in its status, never plain OK.
6. Run the repair twice: the second run must change nothing.
validation: Every link is at the shared position and pinned; its name ends with the site name, or the report lists it as kept unbound with the reason
No bound link was moved: HasSaveablePositions() is false on every link type after the run
No modal dialog during the run; warnings listed in the report
Second run: all rows matched, nothing created, re-placed, moved or removed
bridge_candidate: Test harness pattern: call the add-in's own engine through reflection from run_csharp (mode none), create each deviation in its own transaction, write the report to a file, read state back, run again.

history.lesson: A cloud link can be in the right place and still not be in the state linking produced: Revit records the shared-site association only when it places a link by shared coordinates, and the API cannot set it on an existing instance. Identity of ACC links is not available through the file reference at all. A repair that is to leave nothing behind must identify by cloud GUID, re-create rather than move, and absorb every warning.
history.rule:
1. Identity: loaded link -> GetLinkDocument().GetCloudModelPath() GUIDs; unloaded ACC link -> ExternalResourceReference.GetReferenceInformation() LinkedModelProjectId / LinkedModelModelId (observed 2024.3); file reference only for file-based links; name only when no identity can be read, and never over a link whose identity is known to be another model.
2. Load governed links before checking placement (RevitLinkType.Load); in a batch open all worksets, because a link type on a closed workset cannot be loaded; run with no other open document that has the same links loaded.
3. Placement by shared coordinates = at the shared position AND associated (instance name ends with the site name, not '<Not Shared>'). If either fails: create the new instance with ImportPlacement.Shared FIRST, apply workset and room bounding, pin, verify, then delete the old instance; do it in a SubTransaction and roll back if the check fails.
4. Count annotations that go with the old instance (GetDependentElements filtered to annotation categories) and report them; Delete() also returns internal elements of every link instance.
5. Register an IFailuresPreprocessor on every repair transaction (delete warnings, list them in the report); a run with anything unfixable reports 'OK with N row errors', never plain OK.
6. Run the repair twice: the second run must change nothing.
